title: Pilot
cn: 第 1 集 · 一切的开始
novel:
Ted was an [[architect|architect]] in New York. He drew tall towers all day, yet his own life still felt like an empty room.

One evening his best friend Marshall [[knelt|kneel]] down on the kitchen floor and [[proposed|propose]] to Lily. The small ring [[sparkled|sparkle]]. Lily cried. Ted clapped, smiled, and felt a warm, painful [[envy|envy]]. He was a [[bachelor|bachelor]], and that night the word sounded like a [[curse|curse]].

"Maybe [[destiny|destiny]] needs a push," he said at the bar. Barney laughed. "[[Desperate|desperate]] men tell [[awkward|awkward]] jokes."

Then Robin walked in, wet from the rain. Ted [[stole a glance|steal a glance]], [[rehearsed|rehearse]] three clever sentences in his head, walked over, and [[blurted out|blurt out]] the [[cheesiest|cheesy]] line of his life: "You look like the last page of a book I want to read."

On an [[impulse|impulse]] she said yes to dinner.

Later they stood on a cold [[rooftop|rooftop]]. Below them the traffic [[flickered|flicker]] like a slow river of stars, and on the wet [[pavement|pavement]] a stranger sang badly. Ted [[confessed|confess]] that he was a [[hopeless romantic|hopeless romantic]] who wanted the whole story on the first night.

"Slow down," Robin said.

He never did. But he decided to [[take a shot at|take a shot at]] love — and that one decision took him twenty-five years to explain.

architect.en: a person whose job is to design buildings

kneel.en: to go down so that your knees touch the ground

propose.en: to ask someone to marry you

sparkle.en: to shine with small bright points of light

envy.en: the sad feeling you get when someone else has what you want

bachelor.en: a man who is not married

curse.en: bad luck that seems to come from magic words

destiny.en: the things that will happen to you in the future, which you cannot change

desperate.en: wanting something so much that you will try anything

awkward.en: making people feel shy or uncomfortable

steal a glance.en: to look at someone quickly so that they do not notice

rehearse.en: to practise something before you do it in front of others

blurt out.en: to say something suddenly, without thinking first

cheesy.en: silly and not cool, but in a funny way

impulse.en: a sudden wish to do something without planning

rooftop.en: the top of a building, where you can stand

flicker.en: to shine in a weak way that keeps stopping and starting

pavement.en: the hard path at the side of a road, for people walking

confess.en: to tell someone a truth that you feel shy or sorry about

hopeless romantic.cn: 无可救药的浪漫主义者
hopeless romantic.en: a person who always believes in perfect love, even when it is silly

take a shot at.en: to try to do something, even if you may fail
